open.speaker: pawnbroker
lines: Riverside Pawn. Buy, sell, loan. No guns to anybody I don't know, and I don't know you.
You want the Hallicrafters, it's two hundred and I won't come down, 'cause I know what it is.
It's an SX-100. Two hundred is a steal. Don't tell him.

passives.line: The radio on the shelf is still warm. Someone had it on this morning, and the dial's on no station you know.
A class ring sits alone under the glass with no tag. He's not selling it. He's keeping it.

options.text: No guns. What about shotgun shells?
Somebody had that radio on this morning. Who?

fail.line: A man can listen to his own stock. You want to buy it, two hundred.

shells.speaker: pawnbroker
lines: Carl Ridge. Box of twelve-gauge Monday and another Wednesday. Carl don't shoot deer in February.
I asked what he was after. He said 'nothing that bleeds.' Carl's funny when he's scared.
Two boxes. Four shells under his stand. He's got more than he's saying.

radio.speaker: pawnbroker
lines: Me. Dwight said it picks up something at ten past two, and I didn't believe him, so I sat up with it.
Three notes. Then nothing. Then I unplugged it, and it did it again.
Unplugged. I need that in writing, Lonnie.

slow.speaker: pawnbroker
lines: Slow? Busiest February I've had. Half this town's selling what their daddies left 'em, the other half's buying it in a suit.
I don't like busy. Busy means somebody's leaving.

hub.speaker: pawnbroker
lines: Case is open, register's shut. Go on.

static.line: There's a key under the register. His hand's gone to it twice. Make him give you the key.

options.text: That ring's got no tag, Lonnie. You're not selling it.
Penrose sent us for the ring.
Dwight's driven out to the plant every Thursday since '66.
You could give the coat back.

ring.speaker: pawnbroker
lines: ...No. I'm not. Class of '66, Point Pleasant High, Dwight Mason inside the band.
The suits wanted it before he brought it in. That's not business, that's knowing. I'm holding it till he comes back for it.
He won't. He knows it. So does Lonnie.

ring_fail.speaker: pawnbroker
lines: Everything's for sale in here. That's the sign. Read the sign.
Dwight's wife is out on the Heights, you want to talk rings. I don't.

bluff_ring.speaker: pawnbroker
lines: (He goes very still.) ...So he's got a name now.
Tell Penrose it's gone. Sold it to a fella from Gallipolis, and I don't remember the fella, 'cause I'm good at not remembering.
(He slides a key across the counter.) Back room, bottom drawer. What they bought, I kept a list. You didn't get it here.
He kept a list. Of course he kept a list.

bluff_fail.speaker: pawnbroker
lines: The suits never said that name. Not once in three visits. You just said it in my shop with the door open.
Get out. Come back when you're not working for him. I'll know if you are.

passives.line: That was the right name in the wrong mouth. You hear the bell over the door and it rings like a till.

thursdays.speaker: pawnbroker
lines: Thursdays. I know. He drives past here at dusk every Thursday with the headlights off till the county line.
This Tuesday he pawned the coat, the ring, his daddy's radio, and said 'Not where I'm going, Lonnie.' Tuesday ain't Thursday.
He was early. Twenty-eight years and he was early.
Something moved it up. Something told him the day.

coat_back.speaker: pawnbroker
lines: Give it back. I would. I tried. Drove it out to the Mason place Wednesday and Carol wouldn't open the door.
Said through it, 'He's not cold. He told me he's not cold.' And I drove home with the coat on the seat.
It's on the rack. It's not for sale. The sign's a liar.
She's keeping the door shut on more than the weather, dear.
